Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis

This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- Failing test: CoreOperationTest.testNodeSetOperations asserts that the XPath expression "$array > 0" evaluates to Boolean.TRUE.
- XPath specification excerpt (from the issue): when comparing a node-set with a number, the comparison should be true if there exists at least one node in the node-set whose string-value, converted to a number, satisfies the comparison with the number. Similarly, for node-set vs node-set, the comparison is true if there exists a pair of nodes (one from each set) whose string-values satisfy the comparison.

What the code does:
- CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue and its siblings (LessThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, etc.) implement numeric comparisons by collapsing both operands to a single double each and comparing:
  - CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue:
    - l = InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(args[0].computeValue(context));
    - r = InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(args[1].computeValue(context));
    - return l > r;
  - CoreOperationLessThan and CoreOperationGreaterThanOrEqual behave analogously.

- InfoSetUtil.doubleValue handles node-set-like results as follows:
  - If the object is an EvalContext (which represents a node-set), it calls ctx.getSingleNodePointer() and then converts only that Pointer to a number.
  - EvalContext.getSingleNodePointer iterates contexts and returns the first node pointer it encounters, effectively selecting only the first node of a node-set.

- By contrast, equality is implemented via CoreOperationCompare.equal(EvalContext, Expression, Expression), which:
  - Normalizes Collections to Iterators,
  - Detects Iterator-vs-scalar and Iterator-vs-Iterator cases,
  - Iterates and checks whether any element (or any pair across two iterators) satisfies the equality, matching XPath “any” semantics for node-sets.

Why the test fails:
- The expression "$array > 0" involves a node-set (the array) and a number (0).
- Per XPath, it should return true if any node in the node-set, when converted to a number, is greater than 0.
- Current implementation converts only the first node in the node-set to a number (via getSingleNodePointer and doubleValue), and compares that single number to 0.
- If the first element is not greater than 0 but some later element is, the implementation incorrectly returns false, causing the test to fail.

Conclusion:
- The relational operators (>, <, >=, <=) are implemented with scalar numeric conversion that collapses node-sets to a single node, violating XPath semantics for node-set comparisons.
- Equality uses the correct “any-match” iteration logic via CoreOperationCompare, but the relational operators do not.
- The bug should be addressed by changing the relational operator implementations to:
  - Detect node-set/collection/iterator operands,
  - Iterate over nodes as required,
  - Perform numeric comparisons per node (or across pairs for node-set vs node-set),
  - Return true if any such comparison succeeds.

Impacted code:
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue(EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationLessThan.computeValue(EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationGreaterThanOrEqual.computeValue(EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationLessThanOrEqual.computeValue(EvalContext)

Supporting evidence:
- CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue uses InfoSetUtil.doubleValue on args[0/1].computeValue(context), reducing node-sets to a single double.
- InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(EvalContext) uses getSingleNodePointer, returning only the first node.
- CoreOperationCompare.equal handles node-sets properly by iterating (contains/findMatch), illustrating the correct pattern that relational ops should follow.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

m21.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- Failing test: CoreOperationTest.testNodeSetOperations asserts that the XPath expression "$array > 0" evaluates to Boolean.TRUE.
- XPath specification excerpt (from the issue): when comparing a node-set with a number, the comparison should be true if there exists at least one node in the node-set whose string-value, converted to a number, satisfies the comparison with the number. Similarly, for node-set vs node-set, the comparison is true if there exists a pair of nodes (one from each set) whose string-values satisfy the comparison.

What the code does:
- CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue and its siblings (LessThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, etc.) implement numeric comparisons by collapsing both operands to a single double each and comparing:
  - CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue:
    - l = InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(args[0].computeValue(context));
    - r = InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(args[1].computeValue(context));
    - return l > r;
  - CoreOperationLessThan and CoreOperationGreaterThanOrEqual behave analogously.

- InfoSetUtil.doubleValue handles node-set-like results as follows:
  - If the object is an EvalContext (which represents a node-set), it calls ctx.getSingleNodePointer() and then converts only that Pointer to a number.
  - EvalContext.getSingleNodePointer iterates contexts and returns the first node pointer it encounters, effectively selecting only the first node of a node-set.

- By contrast, equality is implemented via CoreOperationCompare.equal(EvalContext, Expression, Expression), which:
  - Normalizes Collections to Iterators,
  - Detects Iterator-vs-scalar and Iterator-vs-Iterator cases,
  - Iterates and checks whether any element (or any pair across two iterators) satisfies the equality, matching XPath “any” semantics for node-sets.

Why the test fails:
- The expression "$array > 0" involves a node-set (the array) and a number (0).
- Per XPath, it should return true if any node in the node-set, when converted to a number, is greater than 0.
- Current implementation converts only the first node in the node-set to a number (via getSingleNodePointer and doubleValue), and compares that single number to 0.
- If the first element is not greater than 0 but some later element is, the implementation incorrectly returns false, causing the test to fail.

Conclusion:
- The relational operators (>, <, >=, <=) are implemented with scalar numeric conversion that collapses node-sets to a single node, violating XPath semantics for node-set comparisons.
- Equality uses the correct “any-match” iteration logic via CoreOperationCompare, but the relational operators do not.
- The bug should be addressed by changing the relational operator implementations to:
  - Detect node-set/collection/iterator operands,
  - Iterate over nodes as required,
  - Perform numeric comparisons per node (or across pairs for node-set vs node-set),
  - Return true if any such comparison succeeds.

Impacted code:
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue(EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationLessThan.computeValue(EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationGreaterThanOrEqual.computeValue(EvalContext)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationLessThanOrEqual.computeValue(EvalContext)

Supporting evidence:
- CoreOperationGreaterThan.computeValue uses InfoSetUtil.doubleValue on args[0/1].computeValue(context), reducing node-sets to a single double.
- InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(EvalContext) uses getSingleNodePointer, returning only the first node.
- CoreOperationCompare.equal handles node-sets properly by iterating (contains/findMatch), illustrating the correct pattern that relational ops should follow.
